In sharing mode every parsed refresh response reduces to {access_token} plus the injected refresh_token literal: office365-calendar persists refresh_token: "refresh_token" over the real refresh token (spread at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264), salesforce loses instance_url, and expiry fields (expires_in/expiry_date) never reach the stored credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are evaluated at JS runtime as a single literal property name (effectively `"[object Object]"`), and the second one overwrites the first in the object literal. So `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior; in Zod’s default `strip` mode it will accept only `access_token` (and possibly a `"[object Object]"` field) while stripping real fields like `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc. Because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` also injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing, callers like `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` spread `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials, overwriting the real refresh token with the literal string when sharing mode is enabled. Similarly, `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` will drop non-access-token fields from the refreshed token response in sharing mode.
